The Annotated version, supported and recommended since FastAPI 0.95.0, puts Query(max_length=50) inside Annotated and keeps the default as a normal = None. The older style, required before 0.95.0 and still common in existing code, uses Query() itself as the default value, so the default has to go inside it: Query(default=None, max_length=50). For new code, use Annotated: it has multiple advantages and no disadvantages. Make sure you're on at least FastAPI 0.95.1 first, since older versions give errors with Annotated.

c136.question: I'm rendering an item page with Jinja2 templates in FastAPI. How do I pass the item's ID to the template and build a link to that item's URL from it?
c136.answer: Create a Jinja2Templates object (e.g. templates = Jinja2Templates(directory="templates")), declare a Request parameter in the path operation, and return templates.TemplateResponse(request=request, name="item.html", context={"id": id}). Inside the template, call url_for() with the path operation function's name and the same arguments it takes, e.g. {{ url_for('read_item', id=id) }}. This generates the URL handled by read_item(id=id), such as /items/42.

You can also use `url_for()` inside of the template, it takes as arguments the same arguments that would be used by your *path operation function*.

...will generate a link to the same URL that would be handled by the *path operation function* `read_item(id=id)`.

c138.question: How can I override a dependency in FastAPI during testing, and why would I want to do that?
c138.answer: Use the app's app.dependency_overrides attribute, a simple dict: put the original dependency (a function) as the key and your override (another function) as the value, e.g. app.dependency_overrides[common_parameters] = override_dependency. FastAPI will then call the override instead of the original dependency. You'd want this when you don't want the original dependency (or any of its sub-dependencies) to run during tests, and instead want a test-only dependency that provides a value to use where the original one's value was used. To remove the overrides, set app.dependency_overrides = {}; to override only in some tests, set it at the beginning of the test function and reset it at the end.

evidence.quote:
There are some scenarios where you might want to override a dependency during testing.

You don't want the original dependency to run (nor any of the sub-dependencies it might have).

Instead, you want to provide a different dependency that will be used only during tests (possibly only some specific tests), and will provide a value that can be used where the value of the original dependency was used.
For these cases, your **FastAPI** application has an attribute `app.dependency_overrides`, it is a simple `dict`.
To override a dependency for testing, you put as a key the original dependency (a function), and as the value, your dependency override (another function).
And then **FastAPI** will call that override instead of the original dependency.
app.dependency_overrides[common_parameters] = override_dependency
Then you can reset your overrides (remove them) by setting `app.dependency_overrides` to be an empty `dict`:
app.dependency_overrides = {}

If you want to override a dependency only during some tests, you can set the override at the beginning of the test (inside the test function) and reset it at the end (at the end of the test function).
